analysis: Examined base/head of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Tools/FlintNativeProtocolTests.swift. The only changes are test additions: a new test maskCacheKeysIdentifyIdenticalMasksAndOptIntoChaining (head 209-226) asserting FlintNativeProtocolConstraint.allowsChainedDecode is true, maskCacheKey returns nil for remainingTokens 0 and for an out-of-range state (cachedStateCount), and that equal keys map to identical allowedTokenIDs masks; plus head line 267 asserting maskCacheKey is nil after state-pool exhaustion. These are test-only and introduce no runtime behavior themselves. They imply production changes elsewhere in the PR: a mask-cache keyed by an Int and a chained-decode opt-in for the constraint, which affect TB-007 (in-process inference engine) availability and correctness of tool-call constraint enforcement (relevant to T-007 output integrity, and availability per T-029). Integration should verify in the production source: (1) maskCacheKey uniqueness covers mode, allowed tool names/parallel policy and remainingTokens bucket so a cached mask cannot be reused across different requests/constraints with different policies (cross-request mask confusion in batched decode); (2) the cache is scoped per constraint instance or keyed by constraint identity, not shared across tenants such that one request's mask leaks or is misapplied; (3) chained decode still rechecks nextState and fail-closed behavior on state exhaustion (nil key → no cache, empty mask, no EOS); (4) cache size is bounded. Tests cover only a few remaining-token values (1,2,100) and single-constraint key consistency, not cross-constraint collisions. No security regression is visible in this test file.
